obligation: Part 37 event: actual or attempted theft, sabotage, or diversion
citation: 10 CFR 37.57(a) and (c), through the Florida license condition (reports go to the Florida Department of Health, Bureau of Radiation Control)
trigger: Determination that an unauthorized entry resulted in actual or attempted theft, sabotage, or diversion of category 2 material. Part 37 defines sabotage to include deliberate damage to 'the components of the security system' (37.5)
deadline: LLEA immediately after the determination; the State as soon as possible after initiating a response and no later than 4 hours after discovery; written report within 30 days
notify: County sheriff (LLEA); Florida Bureau of Radiation Control (address and telephone in license condition E.2)
applies_at_this_tier: Yes - if a cyber attack is combined with or enables unauthorized entry to the vault

citation: 10 CFR 37.57(b), through the Florida license condition
trigger: Suspicious activity related to possible theft, sabotage, or diversion of category 2 material, for example deliberate tampering with the PACS, cameras, NVR, or IDS communicator, or unauthorized access to the security plan
deadline: Assess without delay; notify the LLEA as appropriate; notify the State as soon as possible but no later than 4 hours after notifying the LLEA
notify: County sheriff (LLEA) as appropriate; Florida Bureau of Radiation Control
applies_at_this_tier: Yes - the main clock for this runbook. The RSO decides; treat attacker activity against security systems as suspicious until shown otherwise

citation: 10 CFR 37.81(b), (d), (f), (g), through the Florida license condition
trigger: A category 2 shipment is lost or missing, or there is actual or attempted theft, diversion, or suspicious activity related to a shipment (for example, the attacker accessed shipment schedules while a shipment was in transit)
deadline: Lost or missing: within 4 hours of the determination (and again if not found after 24 hours). Theft, diversion, or suspicious activity: as soon as possible. Written report within 30 days, except for suspicious activity notices
notify: Florida Bureau of Radiation Control; carrier; receiving licensee
applies_at_this_tier: Yes - only if a category 2 shipment is in transit or scheduled

obligation: Florida report of stolen, lost, or missing sources
trigger: Stolen, lost, or missing licensed radioactive material above the quantities set in the rule
deadline: By telephone immediately (above 1,000 times the labeling quantity, if exposure in unrestricted areas could result) or when still missing after 30 days (above 10 times); written report within 30 days after the telephone report
applies_at_this_tier: Yes if material is found missing during the incident (inventory check in step 3)

trigger: An event involving a source of radiation that might have caused or threatens dose or release above the rule's thresholds (for example, an OT attack that disrupts exhaust ventilation during open waste handling)
deadline: Immediately, or within 24 hours, depending on the threshold
applies_at_this_tier: Yes if the OT attack affects radiological controls

trigger: Breach of security of personal information of Florida residents (employee records, background investigation data)
deadline: No later than 30 days after determination of the breach
applies_at_this_tier: Yes if personal information in SYS-01, SYS-05, or the HR library was accessed

obligation: Florida notice to the Department of Legal Affairs
trigger: Breach affecting 500 or more individuals in Florida
deadline: No later than 30 days after determination of the breach
notify: Florida Department of Legal Affairs (Attorney General)
applies_at_this_tier: Unlikely (about 60 employees plus former employees and applicants); check the count

obligation: Florida notice to consumer reporting agencies
trigger: Notice required to more than 1,000 individuals at one time

obligation: Third-party agent breach notice to the company (inbound)
trigger: A vendor maintaining personal information for the company (HR and payroll SaaS, MSP) has a breach
deadline: Vendor must notify the company within 10 days of determining the breach

citation: State breach notification statutes (all 50 states, DC, PR, USVI; Guam 9 GCA Ch. 48)
trigger: Breach of computerized personal information of state residents (definitions vary by state)
deadline: Varies by state (for example 'without unreasonable delay' or a fixed number of days)
notify: Affected residents; state attorney general or regulator where the state requires it; consumer reporting agencies above state-set counts
applies_at_this_tier: Check residency of affected employees and applicants

trigger: Cyber attack at a licensee subject to 73.54 or 73.110
notify: NRC Headquarters Operations Center via ENS
applies_at_this_tier: No - the company is not subject to 73.54 or 73.110 (P03 G-002). Part 37 events go to the Florida Bureau of Radiation Control, not the NRC Operations Center

obligation: CIRCIA covered cyber incident and ransom payment reports
trigger: Covered cyber incident or ransom payment
deadline: Proposed: 72 hours; 24 hours after ransom payment
applies_at_this_tier: No - final rule not published as of 2026-09-25; as proposed, the company is below the SBA size standard and is not a reactor or fuel cycle facility. Voluntary report to CISA is still encouraged

obligation: OFAC sanctions check before any ransom payment
citation: OFAC Updated Advisory on Potential Sanctions Risks for Facilitating Ransomware Payments (Sept. 21, 2021); 31 CFR ch. V
deadline: Before any payment; full and timely reporting to law enforcement or CISA is a mitigating factor
notify: OFAC (license if sanctioned party); FBI or CISA
applies_at_this_tier: Yes - all U.S. persons. Strict liability for payments to sanctioned parties

obligation: Voluntary report to law enforcement and CISA
deadline: As soon as practical (supports OFAC mitigation)
notify: FBI field office or IC3; CISA

trigger: Cyber incident affecting the customer's data, field laptops used at the customer's site, or work scheduled at the site
notify: Customer supply chain and security contacts

deadline: Per policy (use the carrier's breach hotline before hiring vendors)

citation: FAR 52.204-25 (Section 889) and FAR 52.204-23; FAR 52.240-91(h) in awards under an agency's FAR Part 40 class deviation
trigger: Contractor identifies covered equipment or Kaspersky covered article in use or delivered
deadline: Within 1 business day of identification for covered telecommunications equipment or services (52.204-25(d)); within 3 business days for a Kaspersky covered article (52.204-23(c)); further report within 10 business days in both cases. Under FAR 52.240-91(h) (new awards under an agency's FAR Part 40 class deviation): one report within 72 hours, to https://dibnet.dod.mil for DoD or to the contracting officer for other agencies; a further report within 72 hours of finding missing information.
applies_at_this_tier: No - the company holds no federal contracts or subcontracts
